chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from someone who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his: 'Whoever extends his hand with kindness when he finds the means, Allah will replace for him what he spent in his world, and multiply it for him in his Hereafter.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for spending in the way of Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the concept of *Istibdal* (divine substitution) where Allah replaces spent wealth with something better, a principle deeply rooted in Shia theological discourse on economic justice. It underscores the dual benefit of charity: immediate material restoration in this world and exponential spiritual multiplication in the Hereafter, reflecting the Imam's role in elucidating the practical applications of Quranic teachings.
